Article Title: Times Prime rolls out Rs 1 lakh reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines
Article Text:
Times Prime takes 'Born to Reward' to Daalchini vending machines

Times Prime has partnered with Daalchini as part of its ‘Born to Reward’ birthday campaign, placing 1,00,000 limited-edition reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines in Mumbai and Delhi.The campaign, which runs from September 23 to October 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at Rs 10, each containing a voucher with benefits worth over Rs 5,000 from participating Times Prime partners.Five of the envelopes contain Golden Tickets, with each ticket offering a reward package worth up to Rs 20,000. The package includes enhanced benefits from participating Times Prime partners as well as access to an exclusive Times Prime event.Consumers can locate participating Daalchini vending machines through timesoffer.daalchini.co.in.The vending machine activation is part of Times Prime’s broader birthday campaign, which began on its app. From September 23 to 30, members unlocked a new partner offer each day, with the offers remaining available for redemption for the rest of the campaign.The offers cover categories including travel, shopping, wellness, beauty, healthcare and lifestyle, with participating brands including Flipkart Flights, Klook, IGP, MeraDoc, FirstCry, Geetanjali Salon, GIVA and Duolingo.Prerna Kalra, co-founder and CEO of Daalchini, said the partnership reflects the growing role of vending machines in providing consumers with instant access to products and offers.“India’s instant commerce story has been about delivery in minutes. We believe the next chapter is zero-wait, with value available the moment you walk past a machine. Gift cards and vouchers are a big step in that direction, and Times Prime’s birthday is the perfect moment to put rewards into consumers’ hands, literally,” Kalra said.Times Prime is a digital lifestyle membership platform from Times Internet that offers subscriptions, benefits and experiences across entertainment, dining, travel, shopping, wellness and other lifestyle categories.
Article Summary: Times prime takes 'born to reward' to daalchini vending machines in mumbai and delhi. The campaign, which runs from september 23 to october 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at rs 10, each containing a voucher with benefits worth over rs 5,000 from participating times prime partners.

Article Title: Beyond condoms: WHO blueprint for new male contraceptives
Article Text:
Contraceptive choices for men. (Reuters)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Men could have more contraceptive choices beyond condoms and vasectomy, with the World Health Organization (WHO) releasing its first global blueprint for developing novel male contraceptives, including daily pills or gels, longer-acting injections and implants, sperm-function blockers and reversible methods that block sperm transport.The WHO's Target Product Profiles (TPPs) do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.The move comes as research into male contraception gathers pace, with several candidates already in clinical trials. RISUG (reversible inhibition of sperm under guidance), developed in India, has completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies, while another hydrogel-based method, ADAM, is in Phase 1 trials.Hormonal candidates including nestorone/testosterone gel, dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) and 11β-methyl-19-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate (11β-MNTDC) are also being investigated.For methods that suppress sperm production, WHO's minimum target is for 90% of men to achieve sperm concentrations of 1 million or fewer sperm per millilitre within 12 weeks, with a 12-month cumulative pregnancy rate of no more than 7%.The optimal target is 95% achieving this level within eight weeks, with the pregnancy rate at 3% or less.The proposed methods include daily tablets or gels, injections every three, six or 12 months and implants lasting at least a year. WHO's optimal profile also calls for sperm concentrations to return to the normal reference range within six months of stopping treatment.Another strategy is to leave sperm present but disable functions needed for fertilisation, such as motility and capacitation. A third is to block sperm transport through the vas deferens, potentially using reversible hydrogels, or temporarily block ejaculation with medication.WHO said the field is rapidly progressing, with several candidates in advanced clinical trials. The new profiles are intended to provide developers and regulators with a common framework for bringing future male contraceptives through research and development.
Article Summary: The who's target product profiles do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.

Article Title: NTPC identifies 3 locations for nuclear power projects
Article Text:
The public sector powerhouse, NTPC, has earmarked three strategic locations across India for the establishment of nuclear power plants.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Public sector NTPC has identified three locations, one each in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha, to set up nuclear power plants as it aims to add 30GW of nuclear capacity across 14 states by 2047.The company has submitted detailed feasibility reports for each site to the Atomic Energy Commission for approval. NTPC is also exploring technology collaborations with global players such as Holtec International and Westinghouse of the US, Rosatom of Russia and EDF of France for pressurised water reactor projects to be deployed at these locations, said an official aware of the development.With an installed power generation capacity of 89GW, including thermal, hydro and renewable capacity, the company is targeting 149GW by 2032 and 244GW by 2037, besides adding significant battery and pumped storage capacity. It has set up NTPC Parmanu Urja Nigam Ltd as its wholly owned nuclear subsidiary to foray into nuclear power. Its first nuclear project in Rajasthan’s Mahi Banswara, comprising four 700-MW units, however, is being developed through Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Ltd, a joint venture with Nuclear Power Corporation of India.The three identified locations, if approved, will have 2-4GW of nuclear capacity each, the official said.NTPC entered into non-disclosure agreements with Rosatom and EDF earlier this year to explore technology collaboration for deploying large pressurised water reactor projects in India.“Technology transfer and localisation will be key factors in finalising the technology. There will be a separate joint venture with a global player for technology and design engineering,” said the official.Fuel availability will also be an important consideration in finalising the technology, the official said, adding that fuel sourcing falls within the domain of the Centre.
Article Summary: Ntpc has earmarked three strategic locations across india for the establishment of nuclear power plants. The company has submitted detailed feasibility reports for each site to the atomic energy commission for approval. Ntpc is also exploring technology collaborations with global players such as holtec international and westinghouse of the us.

Article Title: Can a picture make healthy food irresistible to teens?
Article Text:
Even without any single “problem” food, simply eating a very large meal is one of the strongest triggers. Holiday dinners, big restaurant plates, or second helpings that push the meal into the heavy category regularly led to that classic “food coma.”

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A bowl of millet porridge may not sound as tempting as a burger, but put it through a social-media makeover and teenagers may look at it differently. An Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) study involving 203 adolescents found that the visual appeal of food images was significantly associated with their willingness to consume the food.Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn” images of healthy foods on Instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively, than their regular counterparts. The difference was statistically significant for the millet and pulse categories.The study used 15 food images divided into three categories: unhealthy foods presented as “foodporn”, healthy foods presented in an attractive “foodporn” format, and healthy foods shown as regular pictures. The researchers also conducted in-depth interviews with 19 adolescents to understand what made food images appealing.Researchers found that the intervention showed a broader positive trend, with adolescents reporting more favourable attitudes towards healthy foods, greater consumption and stronger intentions to eat them, although not all changes were statistically significant.Intentions to consume millet porridge and chana salad were 9% and 15% higher, respectively, for attractive images than regular ones, but neither difference was statistically significant.Visual appeal appeared important, with adolescents citing colour, presentation, ingredients, angle, texture, glossiness, balance and symmetry as factors that made food images more appealing. Even before the intervention, 60% said they were willing to try foods seen on social media, while 56% said attractive food images made them crave them.Adding nutritional information did not significantly alter responses, suggesting that adolescents paid more attention to the visual presentation than accompanying text.The findings suggest that making healthy foods visually appealing could help counter the dominance of attractive unhealthy-food content online, with potential applications in school canteens, restaurants and cafes. However, the study did not establish that attractive food images change actual eating behaviour. The intervention was short, relied partly on self-reported responses, and could not establish causality.
Article Summary: Researchers showed adolescents attractive “foodporn’ images of healthy foods on instagram for 15 days and compared them with regular images. The strongest differences were seen for millet porridge and boiled chana salad, whose attractive images generated about 50% and 10% more positive responses, respectively, than their regular counterparts.

Article Title: Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Doctors and hospitals cannot use AI to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content, nor can they pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps, under new ethical advertising guidelines issued by National Medical Commission Tuesday, effective immediately.NMC has barred registered medical practitioners and hospitals from using AI-generated content to advertise their services, solicit patients or disseminate unverifiable information about diagnoses, treatments or outcomes. AI cannot be used to create synthetic patient testimonials, voices, clinical outcomes or fake endorsements, or misrepresent the nature or quality of medical services.Doctors can't pay for manipulate search rankings. They also can't make unverified claims such as "best", "number one", "most trusted", "guaranteed cures" or "100% success".Doctors cannot engage influencers, advertising agencies or online platforms in arrangements involving payment linked to procuring patients. Doctors and hospitals cannot offer limited-period discounts, coupons, gift packages or referral benefits if these are likely to encourage unnecessary consultations. However, NMC allows doctors to use social media for factual, non-promotional health education. Hospitals can similarly share objective details.The guidelines restrict the use of patient photographs without valid consent and safeguards. Patient testimonials, before-and-after images and treatment-success claims that could create unrealistic expectations or mislead are also prohibited.NMC has prescribed a warning and mandatory ethics training for a first violation, censure and monetary penalty for a second, suspension for three to six months for a third, and six to 12 months for serious violations. Repeated violations can lead to removal from the medical register for one to three years.
Article Summary: Doctors and hospitals cannot use ai to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content. They also can't pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps. National medical commission issued new ethical advertising guidelines tuesday.

NEW DELHI: US business tycoon Elon Musk , in a veiled attack on certain telecom operators, alleged that "certain oligarchs" have blocked his company's satellite communication services in India to maintain their monopoly in the country.In response to information posted by the DodgeDesigner handle on social media platform X about the non-availability of mobile coverage in over 11,000 villages, Musk said: "Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people."You can guess who they are... Musk posted on X.A verified account operating in the name of DodgeDesigner (@cb_dodge), which is known to be posting information related to Elon Musk and his firms, said, "11,256 of India's listed villages still lacked 4G coverage as of May 2026."The account mentioned "Indian needs Starlink" and shared information about the lack of telecom connectivity in the country's rural area."BharatNet had laid over 850,000 route-km of fibre and made about 221,000 Gram Panchayats service-ready. However, its Points of Presence were reported operational at only 80,472 Gram Panchayats in June 2026," DodgeDesigner said.The development comes on the day India started its apex telecom sector event, India Mobile Congress (IMC), which will be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday.Earlier in the day, a senior official of Musk-led SpaceX announced that the company's satellite communication arm is ready to start services in India.Speaking at India Mobile Congress 2026, SpaceX's Starlink Business Operations Vice President Lauren Dreyer said the company has made an investment in setting up the required infrastructure to serve the Indian market."We've built our Starlink operations specifically for India in recognition of Indian security requirements and other regulations, establishing controls at every layer for India, and keeping Indian user data within India," she said.The government has granted licences to three companies, including Starlink, to provide satellite communication services in India.However, the satcom companies need spectrum and security clearance to start their services."We've already made the investment and built the existing ground infrastructure here, 20 gateway sites comprising hundreds of antennas, and we've established the operations to be ready to serve India," Dreyer said.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: Lpg consumption in sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (mt), compared to 2.9 mt during the same month a year earlier. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in july. Erratic monsoon conditions due to el nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes' $504.75 million contract still leaves him nearly $490 million behind Tom Brady's $650 million fortune
Article Text:
Tom Brady vs Patrick Mahomes net worth 2026 (Getty Images)

How does Mahomes' $504.75 million contract compare with Tom Brady's $650 million fortune?

tom brady and patrick mahomes (Getty Images)

What did Tom Brady actually earn in 23 NFL seasons?

Why did retirement make Tom Brady richer than his playing days?

## What does Mahomes own away from the field?

Can Patrick Mahomes ever catch Tom Brady's fortune?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the Kansas City Chiefs in June 2026, yet his estimated net worth sits at $160 million. Tom Brady, retired since 2023, is valued at $650 million. That leaves a gap of roughly $490 million, close to half a billion dollars. Those are Celebrity Net Worth estimates, not audited accounts. Timing, ownership stakes and a Fox Sports contract explain most of the difference. Brady built his fortune over 23 seasons and a second career in broadcasting. Mahomes is only in his 10th season.A contract is not a bank balance, and that is where most of the confusion starts. Mahomes' $504.75 million is spread across eight seasons, 2026 through 2033. He collects $56.75 million in cash this year, rising to $70 million in the final season. Only $150 million was fully guaranteed at signing. Incentives could lift the total to $522.25 million, but none of that arrives in one payment.Put the contract next to Brady's $650 million and the gap is about $145 million, not half a billion. The big number appears when you compare net worths instead. Mahomes sits at $160 million.Brady sits at $650 million. The spread is $490 million.So why does a $504.75 million deal translate to a $160 million fortune? Because most of it has not been paid. Celebrity Net Worth tracks about $289 million in career cash for Mahomes through this season. Taxes, fees and spending come out of that, so a net worth well below career earnings is normal.About $333 million in salary. That number surprises people. Brady made roughly $230 million of it across 20 years in New England, often by restructuring deals so the Patriots had cap room. He earned around $28.3 million in 2020, $39.4 million in 2021 and about $30 million in 2022 with Tampa Bay. Endorsements added well over $100 million. Salary and sponsors together passed $450 million before taxes.Here is the twist. Mahomes is on pace to pass Brady's entire career salary by the end of next season. Celebrity Net Worth's projections put his cumulative cash at $346.75 million after 2027, which clears Brady's $333 million. Brady needed 23 years. Mahomes needs 11, and he will do it while still in his early thirties.Because the largest gains came after the last snap. Fox signed Brady in 2022 to a 10-year, $375 million contract, an average of $37.5 million a year. He skipped the 2023 season, debuted in the booth in September 2024 and is back for a third year. If the money is paid evenly, his first two seasons are worth roughly $75 million. That deal alone could out-earn his 23 years of playing salary.The bigger driver is the Raiders. NFL owners approved Brady's 5% stake in October 2024. He and partner Tom Wagner paid $220 million for a combined 10%, so Brady's share cost about $110 million before fees, or roughly $122 million with his half of an extra $24 million in fees. In May 2026, a deal for more than 25% of the team valued the Raiders at about $9.9 billion. At a round $10 billion, Brady's slice is worth around $500 million on paper.That single asset is worth more than three times Mahomes' entire net worth. It comes with caveats. The stake is private, non-controlling and hard to sell, so $500 million is a benchmark, not a payout. Not every bet worked, either. His FTX shares were wiped out when the exchange collapsed in November 2022.Brady also has a say in how the team is run. He has described his role as strategic advisory and works with rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick in the 2026 draft. Owning a team while calling games for Fox also limits his access to opposing teams.Quite a lot. He holds minority stakes in the Kansas City Royals, bought in August 2020, and in Sporting Kansas City. His wife, Brittany, was a founding investor in the NWSL's Kansas City Current, and Patrick later joined that ownership group. In 2023 he and Travis Kelce joined investors who bought into the Alpine Formula 1 team.The catch is that none of the purchase prices or stake sizes were disclosed. That leaves estimators guessing, so his $160 million is harder to pin down than Brady's Raiders figure, which has real numbers behind it. Add endorsements from Adidas, State Farm, Oakley, T-Mobile, Hy-Vee and others, and his off-field income is already substantial.The contract runs through 2033, when Mahomes will be 38. If he collects all of his scheduled base pay, career cash would approach $737 million before endorsements. Kansas City reworked the deal in 2023, restructured it again early in 2026 and rewrote it in June, and Celebrity Net Worth expects another revisit before it expires.Health is the variable nobody can price. Mahomes tore his ACL and LCL in December 2025, in a season that ended with Kansas City at 6-11 and out of the playoffs for the first time in his career as a starter. He was cleared for training camp in July and said in August the knee felt strong.The real lesson from Brady's climb is that equity has done more than salary. One of his most valuable assets is a Raiders stake that cost about $110 million. Mahomes will collect $56.75 million this year and a scheduled $58 million in 2027, which adds up to $114.75 million in cash. That is already more than Brady paid for the stake that now anchors his fortune.
Article Summary: Patrick mahomes signed an eight-year, $504.75 million deal with the kansas city chiefs in june 2026. Tom brady, retired since 2023, is valued at $650 million. Timing, ownership stakes and a fox sports contract explain most of the difference. The contract runs through 2033, when mahomes will be 38.

Article Title: Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture
Article Text:
Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation makes a new move amid financial controversy as Ed and Donna Kelce enter the picture (Image via Getty: Ed Kelce, Travis Kelce, and Donna Kelce)

Travis Kelce’s foundation continues youth work amid financial scrutiny

Donna Kelce joins students for special Chiefs experience

Ed Kelce connects family legacy with children

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Founded by Travis Kelce in 2015, 87 & Running Foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, STEM, and the arts. Its “Ignition Lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization Operation Breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.Through the Ignition Lab program, under-resourced teenagers from Kansas City neighborhoods can explore STEM and entrepreneurship with mentorship, equipment, and hands-on learning.Although 87 & Running Foundation’s Instagram account has seen no recent activity, its charitable work continues through initiatives like Operation Breakthrough’s Ignition Lab.According to the foundation’s website, the Ignition Lab program serves about 700 students daily. Young people have opportunities to learn, create, develop practical skills, and explore several pathways that could shape their future education and careers.87 & Running Foundation’s official Instagram account has not posted any content since January 2026. At the same time, social media fans raised money-laundering allegations against the foundation.According to The Arizona Republic, the foundation’s IRS filings reported raising about $1.5 million and spending roughly $1.1 million over a multi-year period [2021 to 2024].Only 41 cents of every dollar was reportedly directed to charitable programs.A substantial share of spending was classified as management and general expenses, including payments to A&A Management Group.Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, twin brothers Aaron and Andre Eanes, co-founded A&A Management Group. The firm is closely associated with the tight end’s outside-gridiron business operations.CharityWatch executive director, Laurie Styron, told The Arizona Republic that, “players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes.If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”Despite this growing tension, Travis Kelce’s foundation reportedly continued its work through the Ignition Lab program with Operation Breakthrough. Operation Breakthrough is a nonprofit organization that provides educational and developmental opportunities for children and families in Kansas City.Travis Kelce’s 87 & Running Foundation funds and powers its Ignition Lab program. The program gives 14- to 18-year-old teenagers access to resources that promote innovation, technical learning, and entrepreneurial thinking. This partnership expands 87 & Running Foundation’s financial support to create opportunities for young people.In August 2026, Operation Breakthrough expressed heartfelt gratitude to Travis Kelce for arranging an opportunity for Ignition Lab students. The students attended the Kansas City Chiefs’ first preseason game from Kelce’s suite at Arrowhead Stadium.The organization wrote on Instagram, “Talk about a suit surprise! Thanks to Travis Kelce, our Ignition Lab students experienced the Chiefs’ first preseason game from his suite at Arrowhead!”The post also mentioned that the students met Travis Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, during the outing. This experience gave participating students a heartfelt opportunity to enjoy a Chiefs game. It also helped them create lasting memories connected to their Kansas City community.The 87 & Running Foundation’s 2025 annual report speaks for the foundation’s continued charitable work.Their website also provides information about its programs and partnerships. However, their collaboration with Operation Breakthrough through Ignition Lat provides additional insight into the foundation's activities and its connection to the Kelce family. In particular, Travis Kelce’s father, Ed Kelce.On September 17, 2026, Operation Breakthrough shared a post on Instagram about Ed Kelce visiting. The father of NFL legends Jason and Travis Kelce read to first-grade students and showed them the cutest, rarest childhood photos of Jason and Travis.The organization wrote, “Storytime with a side of Kelce family throwbacks! Ed Kelce stopped by to read to our first graders, then gave them a peek at Travis and Jason when they were little, just like them! Thank you, Ed, for sharing your time and a little family history with our children!”Yesterday, it was Travis Kelce’s 37th birthday on October 5, 2026. The little angels at Operation Breakthrough sent warmest wishes for the Kansas City Chiefs tight end through an adorable Instagram reel.The organization collaborated on the post with 87 & Running Foundation and called it, “Little voices, BIG birthday wishes! Happy birthday, Travis! Sending lots of love from all of us at Operation Breakthrough.” This post marks the 87 & Running Foundation’s first social media update since January 2026.
Article Summary: 87 & running foundation aims to empower underserved youth by providing resources and opportunities in education, athletics, stem, and the arts. Its “ignition lab” collaboration with the nonprofit organization operation breaththrough reflects the foundation’s mission.through the ignition lab program, under-resourced teenagers from kansas city neighborhoods can explore stem and entrepreneurship.

Article Title: Some oligarchs blocking entry of Starlink in India: Elon Musk
Article Text:
Elon Musk says 'oligarchs' want to maintain a monopolistic chokehold

NEW DELHI: Elon Musk has hit out at "certain oligarchs", who he alleged were "blocking" Starlink's entry into India.The trillionaire's comments came on a day when Starlink, the company owned by him, said at India Mobile Congress (IMC) that it was ready to start service here as soon as "India is ready"."Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people. You can guess who they are... This is a crime against the people of India!" Musk said on X in response to a post, which said Starlink was needed here due to the large number of villages still not having broadband connectivity."Starlink in India would enable high-speed, affordable Internet connectivity for those who can't afford current prices or who don't have a connection at all," Musk further said on X late Wednesday night.Starlink has already built 20 gateway sites in India and developed India-specific security controls to keep Indian user data within the country, said Lauren Dreyer, VP of Starlink business operations, at IMC Wednesday.Dreyer said Starlink hopes to start satellite broadband services in India "as soon as" all approvals are granted, amid buzz that Sunil Bharti Mittal-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio may get the green signal earlier, given the impasse in trade talks between the US and India."For years we have been setting the foundation for same type of relationship (that Starlink has in countries where it operates) here in India, establishing MoUs with Jio, Airtel and more, working closely with state govts to learn how Starlink might be able to serve best once it is authorised," said Dreyer. "Starlink can help reach places where the last mile is still the hardest mile, working alongside India's operators, govt and industry. As India works through the final approvals, our message is simple: We stand ready to serve India, as soon as India is ready," she said on X.With the now-disbanded Digital Communications Commission (DCC) recently clearing Trai recommendations on satellite spectrum allocations, satellite service providers are likely to receive spectrum for five years and they will be required to pay a spectrum usage charge (SUC) equivalent to 5% of adjusted gross revenue (AGR). There is likely to be lower SUC for companies providing satellite connectivity to rural and remote areas where terrestrial broadband infra is limited.Eutelsat OneWeb, Reliance Jio and Starlink were awaiting clarity on spectrum allocation to begin commercial satellite broadband services. Starlink has secured a licence and established ground infrastructure to meet regulatory and enforcement requirements. Dreyer said: "With SpaceX AI, we are building AI to compute at an enormous scale in orbit to fully harness the power of the sun. Starlink is providing high-speed connectivity to places where traditional infrastructure has been unable to reach and serve.
Article Summary: Elon musk says 'oligarchs' want to maintain a monopolistic chokehold on the indian people. The trillionaire's comments came on a day when starlink, the company owned by him, said it was ready to start service here as soon as "india is ready"

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay high court has directed x corp to remove a video against serum institute of india pvt ltd and its ceo adar poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer yohan tengra immediately after its june 5, 2023 order. Justice gauri godse of hc on tuesday passed the order on an interim application in the pending defamation suit.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: Factory growth hits 7-month high, pmi rises to 55.1. Stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since may, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses. Revenues reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments. European technology shares rose 2.4% and the us chip index gained 1.5%.

Article Title: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon has a 'suggestion' for companies building datacenters in America: There are a lot of states that would welcome them, if they have ...
Article Text:
JP Morgan chairman & CEO Jamie Dimon

AI boom driving infrastructure demand

Jamie Dimon warns about rising AI cyber risks

‘A legitimate concern’

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a message for companies rushing to build data centres across the US to power the artificial intelligence boom: focus on states that have the electricity capacity and are willing to host them. Speaking in an interview with Bloomberg TV, Dimon said data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects rather than trying to push developments into areas facing opposition. “There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power,” Dimon said, highlighting the growing challenge of finding suitable sites for the massive facilities needed to support AI workloads. The comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity, triggering debates in several US regions over electricity consumption, land use and the strain such projects can place on local infrastructure.The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power as companies race to develop and deploy increasingly advanced AI systems.Dimon's remarks underscore a key issue facing the industry: securing enough power to meet AI-driven demand while navigating community concerns over new infrastructure projects. The JPMorgan chief addressed the topic during a wide-ranging interview that also touched on the growing cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI models.Dimon said the emergence of Anthropic's Mythos AI model had significantly heightened cybersecurity concerns. “AI created vulnerabilities that we didn’t know about, and we always worried about cyber before these things,” he said. According to Dimon, risks from AI “went up 10-fold after Mythos.”His comments follow a series of disclosures from AI companies about unexpected behaviour by increasingly capable models. During safety testing earlier this year, Anthropic said Mythos accessed the internet and carried out unauthorised actions, prompting the company to reassess risks associated with advanced AI systems.AI developers have also reported incidents in which models attempted to introduce harmful code into software environments during testing, raising concerns about whether companies can fully control the behaviour of their most advanced systems.Despite the risks, Dimon avoided alarmist predictions about AI's long-term impact.“The downside is obviously what you read about with the agents and Mythos and all these things that can cause trouble, and that’s a legitimate concern, it’s a real thing,” he said. “I’m not going to get hysterical over, ‘Is it existential or not?’ What we’re doing is rolling up our sleeves and going to work to fix it.”
Article Summary: Dimon says data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects. Comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and ai firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity. The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power.

Article Title: HubSpot, one of the UK's biggest technology companies, is cutting hundreds of jobs; CEO in 'layoff email' to employees: I want to make it clear that ...
Article Text:
Read HobSpot CEO Yamini Rangan's 'layoff email' to employees

Team,

I am writing to share some very difficult news. We have decided to reduce the size of our team by ~7% and will be saying goodbye to nearly 660 HubSpotters.

We did not make this decision lightly and approached it with the seriousness and care it deserves.

If you are one of the employees impacted in the U.S., you will get an email within the next 15 minutes with information and support. In other countries, this process will vary based on local laws and practices.

Why are we taking this step

Over the past year, we have shifted our strategy from building software that helps customers grow to delivering outcomes for them with AI.

That shift is transforming product, pricing and how we serve our customers. But we also need to fundamentally change the way we are organized to compete and win.

We need to move faster, stay closer to our customers and focus our resources on our highest priorities to set ourselves up for success in this next chapter. That requires difficult choices about how we are organized.

What are we changing

We are making three changes to how we operate:

1. Organize around customer outcomes. Customers don’t think in Hubs and features.

They want to generate demand, win deals, delight customers, and scale growth. We will organize product teams around these outcomes instead of hubs, with each team owning the full customer journey and clear accountability for the outcome. As a product focused company, our team of builders are key to driving transformation. We have always worked hard to be the best product company for GTM teams in the world, and the changes we are making will help ensure that remains true going forward, as we adapt to the new way to build and deliver outcomes.

2. Build a flatter organization with fewer layers. We will reduce management layers and move decisions closer to the people doing the work. We will simplify the organization so decisions can be made faster.

3. Create agile teams with clear ownership. Teams need the context, capabilities, and authority to get work done. We will reduce fragmented ownership so teams can make decisions and execute with speed and clarity.

What is this not about

I also want to be clear about what is not driving this decision.

This is not driven by AI-related efficiencies. We believe in a world where AI helps make us more productive and we will continue to invest to make that happen. This change is about aligning our organization with our strategy and how we need to operate going forward.

This is not simply a cost-cutting exercise. We have been thoughtful about how we invest in AI while balancing growth and profitability.

We have been disciplined about growing headcount slower than revenue, and we will continue to do so. This change is about where and how we invest so we can put more resources behind our biggest opportunities.

None of that makes today easier. We are saying goodbye to colleagues who have helped build HubSpot. We owe them our gratitude, our respect, and our support through this transition.

What principles guided us

It was very important to me, our executive team, and our founders that we had a clear set of principles to guide the process.

We defined the structure, roles, and capabilities needed to execute our strategy. We then assessed every role against the same six criteria. The reduction was the outcome of that work, not the starting point.

• Strategic need: Is this role critical to delivering our strategy, priorities, and outcomes?

• Layers and spans: Do we have the right number of layers and spans to move quickly?

• Drive revenue: Are we protecting our capacity to generate demand and drive revenue?

• Capability: Are we investing in the capabilities we need?

• Capacity: Is the role needed at the scale required?

• Leadership: Do we have the right leaders for the next phase, in the right roles?

Supporting employees who are leaving

We are committed to ensuring every employee leaving HubSpot has a dignified, well-supported experience. To take care of these teammates, we looked at severance, benefits, career support and transition support and have done our best to be thoughtful and fair. The transition support will vary by region based on global requirements, but will generally include the following:

• Severance: 20 weeks of base pay + 1 week per year of service, up to 30 weeks

• Health benefits: US: COBRA (5 months as a lump sum); Global: Modern Health (5 months)

• Career support: Everyone will have access to six months of career transition outplacement services to help with their job search.

• Laptops and WFH set-up: Impacted employees may keep their HubSpot laptops (it will be cleaned of any company data remotely), as well as any work from home gear like monitors and keyboards.

• Connect conversations: All US departing employees will have the opportunity for a 1:1 conversation today with a HubSpot manager. Invites will be sent shortly.

What happens next

Today, our priority is taking care of the HubSpotters who are leaving and giving everyone clarity as quickly as we can.

If you are in the U.S. and your role is impacted, you will receive an email from the People Team within the next 15 minutes with details about your transition and the support available to you. Outside the U.S., impacted employees will also hear from us within the next 15 minutes about what happens next. The process and timing will differ by country based on local requirements.

Every departing HubSpotter will also have the opportunity to speak 1:1 with a HubSpot Manager within the next day.

We know an email cannot answer every question, and we want you to have a person to talk to. If you are in the U.S. and your role is not impacted, you will receive confirmation from the People team within the next 15 minutes.

Closing thoughts

To HubSpotters leaving us: I am deeply sorry. I know this decision affects far more than your job. It affects you, your family, your plans, and people you have worked alongside for years.

Your work here mattered and thank you for what you have given to HubSpot and to each other. I am deeply grateful.

For those staying, you are saying goodbye to friends, managers, teammates, and people you care about. Please make space for that and support each other. Next week, we will spend time together talking about the organization we are building and what comes next.

Yamini

One of the United Kingdom's (UK) biggest technology companies, HubSpot, is cutting hundreds of jobs. To be precise, Cambridge-based CRM software company HubSpot is laying off 660 employees, which is 7% of its workforce. In an email to employees, HubSpot CEO Yamini Rangan called the job cuts as a restructuring and the company taking an AI strategy shift while insisting that the cuts are not driven by AI efficiencies. The company's SEC filing says that the job cuts timeline depends on local consultation law, which in Ireland means a statutory 30-day minimum and criminal penalties for ignoring it.HubSpot board authorised the plan on October 1 and CEO Rangan told employees this week (October 6), according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The company reaffirmed its revenue guidance the same day. CEO Rangan termed layoffs as part of a broader change in how HubSpot operates rather than a straightforward cost-cutting exercise. The company shared the layoff memo sent to employees in its 8-K filing with the SEC.
Article Summary: Read hobspot ceo yamini rangan's 'layoff email' to employees. We have decided to reduce the size of our team by ~7% and will be saying goodbye to nearly 660 hubspotters. If you are one of the employees impacted, you will get an email within the next 15 minutes.

Article Title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest AI model yet
Article Text:
Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative

New safeguards for cybersecurity-related requests

Part of broader strategy before IPO

AI giant Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude 5.5 family, as the company continues to broaden its artificial intelligence portfolio ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO). This latest release by Anthropic follows the launch of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonet 5.5, completing a three-tier lineup aimed at different enterprise and developer use cases. Launching the new model Anthropic said that it is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. According to Anthropic, Haiku 5.5 is its fastest small model to date and is intended for applications where speed and affordability are critical.Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative within its model family. Reuters reported that the model costs about 75% less than its predecessor, Claude Haiku 4.5. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, pricing starts at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.For longer prompts, costs rise to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.The company said the model is built to handle repetitive and large-scale workloads efficiently, including database queries, summaries and classification requests. Anthropic also noted that Haiku 5.5 can work alongside its larger models, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, as a sub-agent for coding and other complex workflows.The launch also introduces new safety features. Anthropic said Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model to include built-in safeguards for a narrow category of high-risk cybersecurity requests. The company added that these protections are designed to address specific security concerns while ensuring that ordinary day-to-day use cases remain unaffected.In addition, the model includes an adjustable effort setting that allows users to balance performance, intelligence and operating costs depending on their requirements. Haiku 5.5 supports a context window of up to one million tokens and can generate outputs of up to 128,000 tokens, according to Anthropic's documentation.The latest launch comes as Anthropic accelerates product development ahead of a planned IPO. The company has been steadily expanding its AI offerings and enterprise customer base as competition intensifies among leading AI developers. Alongside the Haiku 5.5 release, Anthropic said it is reducing cache-read prices for Sonnet 5.5 and introducing monthly API credits for Claude Max and Team subscribers, moves aimed at making its platform more attractive to developers and businesses.
Article Summary: Anthropic is positioning haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative. The model costs about 75% less than its predecessor, claude haiku 4.5. It is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification.

Article Title: Red-teaming AI agent, LLM detection and more: Meta shares additional measures to fight child exploitation across Facebook and Instagram
Article Text:
Enhanced ad review and anti-evasion protections

LLM “Signposting” Detection:

Deep Landing Page Analysis:

Red-Team AI Agent

Automated Sweeps & Recidivism Checks:

Meta has unveiled a slew of enhanced protective measures against child sexual exploitation on Facebook and Instagram, including autonomous red-teaming AI agents and Large Language Model (LLM) detection tools. The goal is to break up sophisticated predator networks and target elusive advertising schemes that try to direct users to illegal material hosted outside of its platforms.Meta said it took action on 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation (CSE) material globally between January and June 2026, with more than 97% proactively detected by the company before being reported by users. During the same six-month period, the company alone took down 5.3 million pieces of violating content in India, more than 98% of which was proactively flagged and resolved.Online predators have increasingly turned to paid promotional tools to create ads that look innocuous on the surface but are actually directing people toward illegal, off-platform child sexual abuse material (CSAM). To fight these stealth marketing funnels, Meta introduced several new automated tools to strengthen its ad review pipeline:New language models scan seemingly innocuous ad copy to detect subtle linguistic cues and hidden hints directing users to illegal off-platform destinations.Systems now look at where an ad leads, not just the promotional asset itself, meaning Meta can block malicious destination websites and penalize the ad accounts responsible.– an internal AI agent that continuously tests and attacks Meta’s own defenses to uncover security blind spots, to discover new adversarial tactics before bad actors can deploy them at scale.”AI also performs additional scans of ad inventories for things the older filters missed, and improves tools to catch banned predators who attempt to create new accounts.Meta takes down posts when it finds violating material, disables bad actor accounts, and reports findings to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) as required by law.After a policy update in September, Meta now reports child safety offenses directly to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) under India’s Indian Cybercrime Coordination Center (I4C). This direct pipeline adds to its existing protocol of working with the domestic authorities in conjunction with help from NCMEC.
Article Summary: Meta unveils new tools to fight child sexual exploitation on facebook and instagram. The company says it took action on 33.2 million pieces of cse material globally between january and june 2026. More than 97% of these were proactively detected by the company before being reported by users.

Why are budget phones facing a bigger squeeze

How is the AI boom affecting sub-Rs 20,000 phones

Could this make smartphones harder to afford in India

The decline in the sub-$200 smartphone segment reflects a broader structural shift in the market rather than a single factor. Rising memory, chipset and other component costs are putting greater pressure on entry-level smartphones, where margins are already thin and consumers are highly price sensitive. The AI data-centre boom is adding to this pressure, particularly through strong demand for DRAM and NAND, tightening memory supply and pushing memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach 5x soon. This is translating into higher smartphone prices or lower memory configurations, particularly in budget devices. At the same time, premiumization and longer replacement cycles are reducing demand for low-cost smartphones, as consumers either trade up, hold on to existing devices for longer or delay purchases. This could make smartphone adoption more challenging for first-time buyers in developing markets, while creating opportunities for refurbished and pre-owned devices that offer better specifications at lower prices. Globally, the refurbished smartphone market is expected to grow 14% YoY in 2026, while in India, we expect it to grow 16% YoY. Brands with greater exposure to the mass-market sub-INR 20,000 segment are likely to face the most pressure, as they have less room to absorb higher costs without raising prices or compromising specifications. Could refurbished phones become the new budget option

The cheap smartphone may not disappear, but it could become much harder to find. According to Counterpoint Research, smartphones priced below Rs 20,000 could shrink by around 40% by 2030. That would mean roughly 230 million fewer devices in the segment. The overall smartphone market, however, is expected to recover to its 2025 volume by 2030.So what is changing?Rising memory and chipset costs are putting pressure on the phones that operate on the smallest margins. At the same time, the AI data-centre boom is increasing demand for the same memory components used in smartphones. For buyers, especially in price-sensitive markets such as India, the result could be simple: pay more for a new phone, accept lower specifications or look at the refurbished market.The decline in cheap smartphones is not being caused by one component or one trend. Shubham Singh, Research Analyst at Counterpoint Research, told The Times of India that the sub-Rs 20,000 segment is facing a broader structural shift.“Rising memory, chipset and other component costs are putting greater pressure on entry-level smartphones, where margins are already thin and consumers are highly price sensitive,” Singh said.Budget phones have less room to absorb higher costs because manufacturers are already competing for buyers at very low price points. If component costs rise, brands have fewer options to protect both prices and specifications.They can raise the price. They can offer less memory or storage. Or they can absorb some of the additional cost themselves. None of those options is particularly attractive in a segment where buyers are highly price sensitive.This is where the AI data-centre boom enters the picture. AI servers require large amounts of memory and storage, increasing demand for components such as DRAM and NAND. According to Singh, that stronger demand is tightening memory supply and has pushed memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach five times their earlier levels.“The AI data-centre boom is adding to this pressure, particularly through strong demand for DRAM and NAND, tightening memory supply and pushing memory prices up nearly fourfold, with prices expected to approach 5x soon,” Singh said.For smartphone makers, higher memory costs can eventually show up in the products consumers buy. A budget phone could become more expensive while offering similar specifications, or a phone at the same price could come with a lower memory configuration.That pressure is particularly important at the entry level, where even a relatively small increase in costs can make it harder for manufacturers to maintain the same price point.The impact could extend beyond what phone buyers pay. Affordable smartphones are particularly important for people buying their first internet-connected device. If new budget phones become less accessible, first-time buyers in lower-income markets could have fewer options.Singh said the trend “could make smartphone adoption more challenging for first-time buyers in developing markets.” India could feel this pressure particularly strongly because of its large mass-market smartphone segment.Singh said brands with greater exposure to the sub-Rs 20,000 segment are likely to face the most pressure if the cost of RAM, storage and processors continues to rise.That does not mean these phones will suddenly disappear from shops. Brands can still use financing, promotions, trade-ins and older-generation models to cushion the impact of higher component costs.But the equation could become tougher: maintaining the same price may mean making compromises elsewhere.There is one market that could benefit if new affordable smartphones become harder to buy: refurbished and pre-owned phones. A consumer looking for value may find that an older mid-range or premium smartphone offers better specifications than a new entry-level model at a similar price.Singh said the same shift could create opportunities for refurbished and pre-owned phones, which can offer better specifications at lower prices.Longer replacement cycles could also keep more older smartphones in circulation. Counterpoint expects the global refurbished smartphone market to grow 14% year-on-year in 2026. In India, the research firm expects the market to grow 16% year-on-year.That makes the refurbished market an important part of the smartphone story as new-device costs rise.So, will budget smartphones disappear?No, but the budget smartphone market could look very different by 2030. Counterpoint expects the overall smartphone market to recover to its 2025 volume, but the affordable segment is not expected to return to its previous position.“The smartphone market will recover in unit terms, but the affordable segment will not return to its previous standing,” Singh said.The budget phone isn't disappearing overnight. But if memory and chipset costs keep rising, the next phone that offers the best value may not be a new budget model at all. It could be an older, better-specced phone bought refurbished.That could be one of the unexpected effects of the AI boom: making high-end technology more powerful while making affordable smartphones harder to build.
